newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ST LUKES MAY SEEK FUNDS - NZ HERALD.
newsitem.headline: ST LUKES MAY SEEK FUNDS - NZ HERALD.

text.p: Shopping mall operator St Lukes Group is tipped to announce a NZ$90 million cash issue or placement this month, the New Zealand Herald said on Friday.
This would give it the capacity to raise a further NZ$40 million in debt, the paper said.
Proceeds of a capital raising were expected to be used for a scaled down expansion of its Glenfield Mall and possibly the Plaza Pakuranga.
St Lukes officials were not immediately available to comment but the company has signalled to the market that it would be seeking further funds to proceed with Glenfield.
Funds may also be earmarked to buy out the other half of the Manakau City Centre that it does not own from National Mutual, the Herald said.
Analysts say that the mall is due for extensive refurbishment. It is likely that St Lukes will want to secure the whole site before any upgrade is embarked on.
The Manukau centre, one of the biggest malls in the country, was valued at NZ$186 million last year, based on a nine percent yield.
But given rental escalations, the price is likely to have appreciated to around NZ$200 million.
Operational management of St Lukes is now in the hands of Australian shopping centre giant Westfield Holdings.
St Lukes, 55.5 percent owned by BT Funds Management Australia, last traded at NZ$1.75 after hitting a record high of NZ$1,83 last month.
